title: Yesterday I went to Plaka
title_target: Χθες πήγα στην Πλάκα — Khthehs pee-ghah steen Plah-kah
goal: Talk about what already happened using the past tense — starting with the fifteen irregular verbs people actually use most.
bekal: learn the past stems of the most common verbs
answer the question Τι έκανες χθες;

dialogs.title: ΔΙΑΛΟΓΟΣ — Telling about yesterday
dialogs.intro: Nikos asks Ana how her day was yesterday. Every verb in this dialog is in the past — and nearly all are irregular, because the most common verbs are always the most bent.

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.id: I went to Plaka with Eleni.
lines.literal: I-went — to-the — Plaka — with — the — Eleni.

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.id: We saw the Acropolis and then had coffee.
lines.literal: we-saw — the — Acropolis — and — after — we-drank — coffee.

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.id: Yes, we ate at a taverna. It was delicious.
lines.literal: yes, we-ate — in — a — taverna. it-was — very — tasty.

lines.speaker: Νίκος:
lines.id: What time did you get home?

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.id: I got back at eleven. I was very tired.
lines.literal: I-came — at-the — eleven. I-was — very — tired (f).

lines.speaker: Νίκος:
lines.id: So you had a good day!

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.id: Very good. I took some photos, too.
lines.literal: very — good. I-took — also — some — photos.

notes: **The past tense has the same endings for ALL verbs, no exceptions: -α, -ες, -ε, -αμε, -ατε, -αν.** This is the best news in all of Greek grammar. Only the stem has to be learned; once you know the "I" form, the other five come free.

**The past stem is often far from the everyday form**, and the fifteen most common verbs are the most bent: πηγαίνω → **πήγα**, βλέπω → **είδα**, τρώω → **έφαγα**, πίνω → **ήπια**, λέω → **είπα**, έρχομαι → **ήρθα**, παίρνω → **πήρα**, βρίσκω → **βρήκα**. ⚠️ There's no shortcut; this part simply has to be learned.

**But you're already halfway there.** These stems are nearly the same as the forms after **να** you learned in unit 12: να **πάω** → **πήγα**, να **δω** → **είδα**, να **φάω** → **έφαγα**, να **πιω** → **ήπια**, να **έρθω** → **ήρθα**, να **πάρω** → **πήρα**. One thing to learn, two places to use it.

⚠️ **Past-tense stress always falls on the third syllable from the end.** That's why short words grow a prefix **έ-** or **ή-** to give the stress somewhere to sit: γράφω → **έ**γραψα, τρώω → **έ**φαγα, πίνω → **ή**πια. And once the word gets longer, the prefix disappears again: **έ**φαγα but φ**ά**γαμε; **έ**γραψα but γρ**ά**ψαμε. Watch this shift in the dialog: *ήπιαμε*, *φάγαμε*, *είδαμε*.

**Ήμουν and είχα are the two past forms you'll need most.** *Ήμουν κουρασμένη* — I was tired (yesterday). *Είχα καλή μέρα* — I had a good day. ⚠️ The "he/she" and "they" forms are both **ήταν**, just as είναι covers two lines in the present.
**Ήταν is also used for things and situations:** *Ήταν πολύ νόστιμο* (it was delicious), *Ήταν ωραία* (it was lovely). That second sentence is the standard answer to "how was yesterday?".
**Λοιπόν (*lee-POHN*) = "so, well then"**, the most common linking word in Greek conversation. It's also used alone as *Λοιπόν;*, meaning "and?" or "so what's up?".
**Μερικές φωτογραφίες = some photos.** Μερικοί, μερικές, μερικά agree in gender and are always plural. It's a cousin of μερικές φορές (sometimes), which you already use.

grammars.title: Past-tense endings — the same for every verb
body: Take a past stem, stick on these six endings, done. No groups A, B, or Γ here; the past tense levels them all.
after: ⚠️ Note the **εμείς** and **εσείς** lines of έφαγα: the έ- prefix drops because the word is now long enough to carry the stress. In πήγα and είδα the stress is part of the stem, so nothing changes.
To negate, **δεν** still goes in front: *Δεν πήγα.* *Δεν είδα τίποτα.* No helper word like English *did*.

grammars.title: Fifteen past stems to learn by heart
body: Everything on this list is irregular or nearly so — and all are among the hundred most common words in Greek. The regular ones are waiting in the next unit.
after: **Ήμουν in full:** ήμουν, ήσουν, **ήταν**, ήμασταν, ήσασταν, **ήταν**. **Είχα in full:** είχα, είχες, είχε, είχαμε, είχατε, είχαν — exactly the same endings as other verbs.
⚠️ **Είδα and είπα are easy to mix up** because they look alike and both start with ει-. One means saw, the other said. Memory trick: **δ** as in *δες* (look), **π** as in *πες* (say).

rows: Did you have a good time?

items: **Πήγα στην παραλία.** — I went to the beach. · **Έμεινα σπίτι.** — I stayed home.
**Ήταν πολύ ωραία.** — It was really lovely. · **Ήταν λίγο βαρετό.** — It was a bit boring.
**Πέρασα τέλεια!** — I had a great time! · **Ήμουν κουρασμένος / κουρασμένη.** — I was tired. ⚠️ The ending follows your own gender: -ος for men, -η for women.
**Δεν έκανα τίποτα.** — I didn't do anything. An honest and very common answer.
**Χθες / προχθές / την περασμένη εβδομάδα / πέρσι** — yesterday / the day before yesterday / last week / last year.

blocks.title: If you climb up to the Acropolis
items: **Η Ακρόπολη** literally means "upper city" — ἄκρος (top) + πόλις (city). The same words gave English *acrophobia* and *metropolitan*.
**Ο Παρθενώνας** is the temple on top, from παρθένος (maiden) — a title of the goddess Athena. The city name **Αθήνα** really does come from the goddess's name, not the other way around.
⚠️ Go up **πολύ νωρίς το πρωί** or **πριν το κλείσιμο** — the Athens noon sun on shadeless white marble is no joke. *Πάρε νερό και καπέλο* — bring water and a hat.
**Ήταν εντυπωσιακό!** (*ehn-dee-poh-see-ah-KOH*) — "it was so impressive!" One word worth learning for that moment.

exercises.prompt: Change to the past tense, same subject.
Fill in ήμουν, ήταν, or είχα.
Put the words in the right order.

items: Yesterday I went to the beach.

answers: πήγα — είδες — έφαγε — ήπιαμε — ήρθαν — πήρατε
Τι έκανες χθες; — Πήγα στην Πλάκα. — Μετά ήπιαμε καφέ. — Τι ώρα ήρθες; — Ήταν πολύ ωραία.
Χθες πήγα στην παραλία. — Είδαμε την Ακρόπολη. — Έφαγα σε μια ταβέρνα. — Ήμουν πολύ κουρασμένος. — Πώς ήταν;
